category_title: Chamorro 5th-grade student with ADHD and literacy struggles who equates reading with pronunciation
minimal_context: Juan is working on a writing assignment in a small group setting and is asked to edit his story.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please write down your ideas for the story on your sheet of paper, and then review it to see what changes you can make.

STUDENT: (Quickly scribbles a few words on the paper) Done! I finished it already.

TUTOR: Let's look at your story. What can you add to make the ideas more cohesive?

STUDENT: (Erasing a word and rewriting it) I’ve seen my writing... My penmanship is not so good. I need to practice it.

TUTOR: We can worry about the handwriting later. Let's focus on adding more sentences to the story right now.

STUDENT: But Pedro always gets A’s for penmanship on his report card... I want to get A’s, too. I don't need to add more, I just need to make these letters look neater.

options.A: Praise the student's positive behavior as a component of proactive and preventive classroom management during writing tasks.
options.B: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during writing instruction and small group activities.
options.C: Address the refinement of content and mechanics during the writing process, from first draft to final copy.
options.D: Observe occurrences of the target behavior during the writing class, recording data in scatter plots and ABC charts.
